included: §1 Remove whole-character hiding (hidePresenceAsSpoiler, hideProfileAsSpoiler, includeHiddenProfiles, revealHiddenProfile, excludeHiddenProfiles) across UI, queries, services, repositories, DTOs, create/update/read, mappers, aggregates, search, series
§1 Remove presence gating by firstAppearance*/contextPage on roster, details, edit, counts, search, series, keeping ownership, soft-delete, book access and series context (allowedBookIds)
§1 Prisma migration dropping both columns without losing characters, links, media, roles or names
§1 Remove the hide-presence switch, its hints and the hidden-characters badge; keep the hidden-fields lock badge on cards
§1 Book edit form opens and saves; post-save navigation lands on reachable details
§2 Seven book-field spoilers: masking table, fallbacks, manual reveal (incl. missing displayName and portrait reveal), no DOM/API leak before reveal, reveal not persisted
§2 'No value, no spoiler': disabled+unchecked switches, reset on clear in form and payload, stale-flag normalization on normal edit, no indicators for stale flags
§3 Roles: per-role flag kept, one group reveal, no count, no FE re-filter
§4 Aliases: two independent groups (global / context book), independent reveal keys and hidden markers, global profile masks spoiler global aliases server-side, owner editor gets full data
§5 Spoiler section UX: no Collapsible, all seven rows visible in two ordered groups, short hints, reuse ActionRow/Switch/Separator/EditSection/ScopeBadge
§6.5 OpenAPI + Orval regeneration, targeted checks, typecheck/lint
§7 Acceptance criteria (as doneWhen and test tasks)
'Не робити' list (as doneWhen guards and exclusions)
excluded: isUnreliableNarratorSpoiler, form/image spoilers (CharacterForm.isSpoiler), timeline, theory and relationship spoilers (hideRelationshipAsSpoiler, isTypeSpoiler, isDescriptionSpoiler, introduced* reading-position gate on edges): 'Не робити' #1. Only the dependencies on the two removed flags are touched (T5, T6)
New tables, reveal endpoints, feature flags, reveal state in localStorage/URL, a 'Керувати прихованими' UI, reveal buttons on cards: 'Не робити' #2, §1, §2, §3
Mass data migration that rewrites stale *IsSpoiler=true flags with empty values: §2 'не роби окремої масової data-міграції'
Redesign of lists, cards or the global catalog; catalog filters hasSpoilers/includeSpoilerSearch keep their semantics apart from dropping the hidePresenceAsSpoiler predicate: 'Не робити' #2

Series profile alias and role masking (series-characters.service.ts:130-136, character.mapper.ts:612): §3 and §4 scope book details and the global profile only. Series surfaces only lose presence gating (T8)
Merge preview hasHiddenRecords (characters.ts:873, character-merge.service.ts:122): a different concept (spoiler records on the loser). Only its hidePresenceAsSpoiler predicate goes (T5)
docs/features/characters.md (lines 22, 43, 76, 82, 86 describe hidePresenceAsSpoiler): not requested by the spec; it goes stale and should be refreshed in a follow-up
Changelog entry: not requested by the spec

openDecisions.question: What are the names of the two alias-group reveal and hidden keys, and does the old 'aliases' key survive?
openDecisions.specSays: §4: 'globalAliases та bookAliases або рівнозначне точне найменування' instead of one 'aliases'; hiddenFields keys or equivalent, no count.
options: A. globalAliases + bookAliases in CharacterRevealFieldKeySchema and as hiddenFields markers. 'aliases' is removed
B. The same names, with 'aliases' kept as a deprecated alias that reveals both groups
openDecisions.codebaseCost: Reveal state is component useState (character-details-page.tsx:366), not URL or storage, and the only client is the Orval client regenerated in the same PR. 'aliases' is read in 3 places: assembler :99, view mapper :76, character-edit-form.ts:207. i18n already has characters.page.globalAliases / bookAliases labels (uk.json:8135, :8148).
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Nothing persisted depends on 'aliases', and keeping it re-creates the over-broad reveal the spec removes.
openDecisions.answerNote: Accepted as stated assumption (user did not object)

openDecisions.question: How far does removing reading-position presence gating go?
openDecisions.specSays: §1: presence is not gated by firstAppearance*/contextPage 'на всіх поверхнях персонажів' (roster, details, edit, counts, search, series). 'Не робити' #1: do not change theory/other spoilers except dependencies on the removed flags.
options: A. Drop positionGate from ReadingContextWindow entirely. Character presence everywhere, groups and theories included (collectUnreachableCharacterIds: character-groups.service.ts:439, character-theories.service.ts:241), uses only allowedBookIds. Remove contextPage/Chapter/AudioSeconds from the characters, groups and theories query schemas, and delete the FE readingContext plumbing. Relationship, graph and path keep their own introduced* gate
B. As A for the character surfaces, but groups and theories keep position gating of member/target characters and their reading-position params
C. Keep every param in the schemas and ignore it on the server
openDecisions.codebaseCost: No FE code sends reading position to groups or theories (only features/characters/** sends it), so their gate is dormant API behaviour. A removes reading-position.ts usage from reading-context-window.ts entirely. B keeps a second window shape alive for two dormant callers. C leaves dead params in OpenAPI.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. The spec's premise is that a character's existence is never hidden. Group and theory gating of a member's presence is that same rule, not a theory-content spoiler.
openDecisions.answerNote: User answer 2026-10-15: remove everywhere incl. groups and theories

openDecisions.question: How does the owner editor get full data while the normal view stays masked?
openDecisions.specSays: §4: separate the normal view from full owner editing within the existing API and hooks. A minimal mode param on the existing endpoint is allowed only if server masking of global aliases is otherwise impossible. No new endpoint.
options: A. No new param. The no-context path masks by default and honours the existing revealFieldIds. The editor keeps sending every reveal key (it already sends ALL_REVEAL_FIELD_KEYS, character-edit-page.tsx:58-63), and with bookId it goes through the contextual path with everything revealed
B. A minimal mode param (e.g. view=edit) on GET /api/characters/:id that returns the unmasked owner row in both scopes
openDecisions.codebaseCost: A needs zero contract additions. ALL_REVEAL_FIELD_KEYS derives from the enum, so new keys flow in automatically. Book aliases are replaced per bookId (characters.repository.ts:1094), so restricting the book group to contextBookId cannot drop other books' aliases. B adds a param, a branch in the service, an OpenAPI change and a hook flag.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Server masking is achievable without a param, so by the spec's own condition the param is not justified.
openDecisions.answerNote: Accepted as stated assumption: no mode param, editor sends all reveal keys

openDecisions.question: In the normal global-profile response (no contextBookId), are per-appearance book spoiler values masked too?
openDecisions.specSays: §4: mask spoiler global aliases and leak no other books' aliases. §2: masking is required 'в контекстній відповіді API'. The global profile is not contextual.
options: A. Mask every appearance through toMaskedBookCharacterView with the request's revealFieldIds
B. Mask only aliases. Appearances stay unmasked, as today (toDetailsView, character-view.mapper.ts:40-47)
openDecisions.codebaseCost: The global page renders only title, series, importance and POV per appearance (character-details-page.tsx:81-143), so A changes no UI. A reuses mapMaskedAppearance (:118-131). Today the global response ships every book's spoiler description, impression and notes to the browser.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. It costs nothing, closes the API leak, and the editor still gets everything under D3-A.
openDecisions.answerNote: Accepted as stated assumption: global response masks per-appearance book values

openDecisions.question: Where do the new reveal actions for the book name and portrait go in details?
openDecisions.specSays: §2: add the missing reveal actions for name and portrait in details, reuse CharacterSpoilerField, no new components.
options: A. Two CharacterSpoilerField rows at the top of the book section, rendered only while hidden. After reveal the header shows the book name and portrait
B. A small reveal control inside DetailsHeader (:405-472) next to the name and avatar
openDecisions.codebaseCost: A is the same SpoilerText pattern as the other five (:221-260). B needs header layout work and a second visual pattern.

openDecisions.question: Wording of the hidden status in details
options: A. A literal 'Статус приховано' placeholder via an optional hidden-text prop on CharacterSpoilerField
B. Keep the current pattern: the 'Статус' label above the generic 'Приховано (спойлер)' (character-spoiler-field.tsx:29-36, uk.json:8223)
openDecisions.codebaseCost: B is zero work and matches the other six fields. A adds a prop and a key.
openDecisions.recommendation: B, unless the user wants the literal text. Label plus placeholder already reads 'Статус: Приховано'.
openDecisions.answerNote: User answer 2026-10-15: keep the same pattern as other fields (label Статус + Приховано (спойлер))

openDecisions.question: How is species shown in contextual details?
openDecisions.specSays: §2: when the override is hidden, the effective species is character.species. When the override is available and not hidden, the book value takes priority. Global data must not change its semantics.
options: A. Keep the current split: global species in ProfileSection (:663-665) and the override as its own revealable 'Вид у цій книзі' field in the book section (:253-260)
B. ProfileSection shows the effective species (the visible override, else global) in book context
openDecisions.codebaseCost: A is zero work and keeps the global profile's semantics. B changes ProfileSection in book context only.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. The book section is where the book value has priority, and the profile section stays global data.
openDecisions.specRef: §2 table row speciesOverrideIsSpoiler; paragraph after the table
openDecisions.answerNote: User answer 2026-10-15: keep two separate fields

openDecisions.question: Does the server also coerce a stale flag to false on write?
openDecisions.specSays: §2: reset 'у формі та у payload'. Normalize 'форму й запис при звичайному редагуванні'. No mass migration.
options: A. FE only: form and payload normalization (T23), plus value-aware masking on read (T14)
B. Also coerce in buildBookCharacterUpdateData when a payload sends an empty value with a true flag
openDecisions.codebaseCost: UpdateBookCharacter is a partial PATCH (characters.ts:309-342). Coercing a flag sent without its value needs a read-before-write. B covers only the case where both arrive in the same payload.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. The editor sends the full profile on every save (character-edit-form.ts:458-481), and T14 already suppresses indicators for stale flags.
openDecisions.answerNote: Accepted as stated assumption: FE-only normalization + value-aware masking on read

GET /api/books/:bookId/characters/:characterId (no FE consumer) now returns the masked contextual view (contextBookId = bookId, optional revealFieldIds query), covering every appearance inside the series window up to this book; 404 if the character has no appearance in this book. Security-review fix (spec §7: no hidden values in a reader-context API response).

Series window kept on FE (spec §7 "контекстне обмеження книг серії"): the old toCharacterReadingContext is reduced to toCharacterBookContext, which sends contextBookId under the exact old condition (book not finished/dnf and currentPage > 0) without any reading-position params; details/edit keep contextBookId from the URL.
hiddenContent.hasHiddenNodes removed from the graph view contract: after T6 it was constantly false and had no FE consumer.
Global GET returns character forms in full as before ("Не робити" #1: form/image spoilers unchanged).

Details pages use placeholderData: keepPreviousData so a reveal refetch keeps the masked page in place instead of flashing a skeleton; components are keyed by characterId[:contextBookId] so reveal state never carries across characters/books.

Focus management after reveal (focus moves to the revealed content, pending reveal button stays focusable with aria-busy) and distinct accessible names for the two alias reveal buttons were added after the accessibility audit (WCAG 2.4.3 / 4.1.3).
statusCustomText is returned only when the visible status is "other" (stale text after a status change is never sent). Security-review fix.
residualLimitations: unreliableNarrator stays flag-only masking (not value-aware): spec "Не робити" #1 forbids changing that spoiler.
Series profile appearance points drop spoiler roles without a roles marker (series surface has no reveal UI; spec forbids new card-level reveal buttons).

Pre-existing, not from this diff (a11y audit 2026-10-15): importance badge «Центральний» contrast 3.92:1 (Badge primary variant, vendored ui); Switch focus ring 2.07:1 (global --ring token); role picker combobox aria-controls points to a missing id.
Pre-existing: a failed details fetch (network error) renders the "character unavailable in this book" state instead of an error; with reveal it drops the page to that state too.
